title: Crown and Ember
premise: August Okafor has guarded the sealed Ember Gate for seven years, selling harmless charms in a city where magic is a hanging offense. When a prophecy written a century ago names tonight's date—her, a scholar named Wren—as the one who will reopen the gate, August must choose between the law that keeps the peace and the truth that the usurper's armies are marching on a lie. Together they uncover that the 'ancient war' was manufactured by the usurper's line to justify outlawing magic and hoarding its power. In the end, August opens the gate not to unleash war but to return magic to the people it was stolen from, sacrificing her guardianship—and nearly her life—while Wren chooses love over the scholarly duty that first bound them to the prophecy.
about_author: Tamsin Underhill is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing forbidden manuscripts before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a drafty coastal cottage, accompanied by an opinionated cat named Marginalia.

chapters.title: The Keeper of Small Charms
chapters.summary: August's POV. We meet her double life: licensed charm-seller by day, secret keeper of the warded Ember Gate beneath the city by night. She performs a routine sealing ritual, weary but dutiful. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as contentment—the calm before prophecy strikes.

chapters.title: A Date Written in Ash
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A junior archivist, Wren discovers a century-old prophetic codex whose final entry names tonight's date and describes a stranger with August's exact scar. Their supervisor confiscates the page. Emotional beat: fascination curdling into dread as Wren realizes the prophecy is already in motion.

chapters.title: The Stranger at the Threshold
chapters.summary: August's POV. Wren arrives at August's charm shop seeking the woman from the codex; mid-conversation, the Gate flares for the first time in seven years, pulling them both down into its vault. Emotional beat: reluctant collision of two strangers bound by something neither chose.

chapters.title: What the Gate Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Inside the vault, the Gate shows them visions: a war that never happened, staged battles, a royal bloodline built on fabricated heroism. Emotional beat: vertigo of learning history itself is the usurper's oldest forgery.

chapters.title: Laws Written in Fear
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They surface to find the city under curfew; the usurper's inquisitors have arrived hunting 'gate-touched' citizens. Wren burns their own archive credentials to cover August's tracks. Emotional beat: first act of treason, thrilling and terrifying.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Debt
chapters.summary: August's POV. Flashback chapter: how August inherited the Gate from her executed mentor, and the promise she made never to open it. Now she understands the promise was built on the same lie. Emotional beat: grief reframed as betrayal.

chapters.title: Ink and Iron
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The pair decodes the codex's cipher using Wren's scholarship, learning the Gate doesn't start wars—it returns stolen magic to those it was taken from. Emotional beat: intellectual intimacy deepening into trust, then something warmer.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Hound
chapters.summary: Inquisitor-General Corvane's POV. A cold, believing antagonist who genuinely thinks magic must stay caged. He traces the vault flare to August's district. Emotional beat: menace without caricature—a man certain he is the hero.

chapters.title: Sanctuary of Thieves
chapters.summary: August's POV. They flee to the Undermarket, a black-market haven of unlicensed magicians August once protected. Old debts are called in; some refuse to help. Emotional beat: loyalty tested—her years of quiet kindness buy shelter, but not unity.

chapters.title: The Free Cities' Silence
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. An envoy reveals the free cities know the armies are coming and plan to surrender rather than fight. The prophecy may be their only weapon. Emotional beat: despair at institutional cowardice; justice must come from outside the law.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: August's POV. Captured briefly, August is offered amnesty if she surrenders the Gate's key-stone. She escapes with Wren's help but learns Corvane knows about the codex. Emotional beat: temptation of safety versus the weight of truth.

chapters.title: Night on the Salt Road
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Fleeing toward the Gate's sister-shrine, August and Wren finally speak plainly about what's growing between them—and agree that after this, duty comes first. Emotional beat: love confessed and immediately deferred, bittersweet.

chapters.title: The Shrine of Hollow Kings
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At the sister-shrine they find proof carved in stone: the founding dynasty stole magic from every household in the realm. Wren makes rubbings and copies—the evidence that could turn cities. Emotional beat: awe and fury; truth has a physical weight.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Undermarket
chapters.summary: August's POV. A friend sells their route to Corvane to save his own children. The shrine evidence is seized; Wren is captured. Emotional beat: heartbreak—loyalty vs. survival has no clean answer, and August cannot hate the betrayer.

chapters.title: The Trial of Wren Vale
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Publicly tried for heresy, Wren uses the courtroom to recite the stolen history aloud before the inquisitors can silence her. Riots spark in the gallery. Emotional beat: courage as contagion—one voice making truth contagious.

chapters.title: Ember Rising
chapters.summary: August's POV. With the Undermarket's remnants, August storms the prison convoy. Corvane, shaken by the riots, begins doubting his own doctrine. Emotional beat: rescue as rebellion; the lawless doing what the law would not.

chapters.title: The Armies at the Wall
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The usurper's vanguard reaches the free cities, revealing even Corvane was expendable—he was always meant to die holding the door. Emotional beat: the true believer's crisis as he glimpses the machinery using him.

chapters.title: Key-Stone
chapters.summary: August's POV. At the Gate, August faces the choice: keep it shut and let the cities fall slowly, or open it and return magic to everyone—including enemies. Wren begs her to find a third way. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized—loyalty to a promise vs. loyalty to truth.

chapters.title: The Opening
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. August opens the Gate as the armies breach the walls. Magic floods back to the common people; soldiers drop weapons as power they never knew was theirs wakes in their hands. August is nearly consumed by the Gate. Emotional beat: climax—sacrifice, chaos, and terrible beauty.

chapters.title: What Corvane Chose
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Facing the reopened Gate and the usurper's order to burn the city regardless, Corvane turns his inquisitors against the army instead, buying the city hours. He falls. Emotional beat: redemption through defection—an enemy choosing justice over obedience.

chapters.title: After the Fire
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The usurper's line collapses; the free cities convene to write new law with magic in the open. Wren publishes the codex uncensored, refusing a post in the new government. Emotional beat: exhaustion and hope; truth outliving both its martyrs and its keepers.

chapters.title: Crown and Ember
chapters.summary: August's POV. August survives, freed from guardianship, her scar now a mark citizens touch for luck. She reopens the charm shop—not hiding anymore—with Wren beside her. Emotional beat: resolution—love chosen over duty at last, and a gate that stays open because it no longer needs guarding.
